key_insight: A self-consistent statistical mechanics model predicts the final stationary vorticity state of a sheared 2D Euler fluid, revealing a robust core-halo structure with a population-inverted core.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to anticipate long-time shear-flow outcomes in inviscid 2D turbulence without directly simulating the full time-dependent Euler dynamics.
method: Build a self-consistent ansatz for the Vlasov equation.
Infer the stationary stream function from non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
Predict the asymptotic vorticity distribution and resulting core-halo structure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical demonstration of stationary-state prediction and a qualitative match to the expected relaxation outcome, rather than a data-driven benchmark.
watch_item: The framework appears tailored to idealized inviscid 2D Euler/Vlasov dynamics, so extending it to viscous, noisy, or fully 3D flows may require additional modeling.
paper_title: Predicting the Final Stationary State of Sheared 2D Euler Fluids
